components.gap: Complete this source-specific component at the fixed identity and bounded scope: the original abstract-model-theory axioms and the selected Lindstrom-theorem formulation/proof bridge of Barwise 1974 (held version of record, ACQ-2026-10-0032), retaining the actual closure conditions and any differing logic convention. Missing items, compared with the source: (1) The category of all languages is not fully defined: the general composition of k-term interpretations (a unary interpretation with term c followed by a binary one with terms t, t' gives a ternary interpretation with terms g(t,t'), t, t', g the image of c; 'the general definition is entirely analogous'), the identity morphisms, hom_k and k-morphisms, and the fact that a k-morphism composed with an l-morphism is a (k+l)-morphism (Part I, 4.1-4.2, pp. 229-230) are absent; only the composite with an inclusion is given (w02c-p02-003 body lines 280-284), so the functor that the axioms require is underdetermined. Lemma 4.3 (i)-(ii) (monomorphism iff one-one; epimorphism iff retraction iff onto, p. 230), Lemma 5.5 (ii)-(iii) (p. 233), the motivation of Section 6 by admissible fragments and Example 6.1 (the categories C_kappa, p. 233) and the reasons Definition 6.2 is called tentative (other closure conditions; problem P6, p. 234) are absent. (2) The justificatory account of the axioms is absent: the Section 1 summary that a logic must make elementary syntactic operations (renaming, relativizing) performable and give isomorphic structures the same sentences, that free variables are replaced by constant symbols, and that the functor notion makes this work (p. 224); and the Section 7 account (axioms reached by trial and error from considerations (i)-(iii); no single result needs all conditions; generality versus intuition; the functor 'at the heart of the syntax', p. 234). (3) The remaining Section 7 consequences are absent: 7.2 for every inclusion L subset K (the text has only the case L = L_phi, body lines 140-144), 7.4 (onto interpretations in a full subcategory, p. 236), 7.5(ii), the definition of logical equivalence and its independence of L (p. 236), and the remark with example that 7.5(ii) cannot be improved to phi = psi (p. 237). (4) Definition 3.1's 'stronger than' (L# > L*, p. 257) is not defined although the text uses it (body lines 9, 436-437). (5) Historical, justificatory and normative claims of the Lindstrom formulation are absent: the Section 3 opening (Lindstrom characterized L_omega-omega as the strongest logic with the compactness theorem and the Lowenheim property; the significance of this for extensions of L_omega-omega; Barwise's characterizations are obtained 'by pulling Lindstrom's proof apart at the seams', for every kappa = beth_kappa, in particular kappa inaccessible, p. 257; the text instead calls the route 'of its own', body lines 5-6); the attribution of 3.4 to Lindstrom's papers [8, 9] (p. 259); Barwise's judgment that Lindstrom's class-based approach is unsatisfying on two grounds and the stated main purpose of the notes (p. 259; def:p03-w03-p03-048-versus-lindstrom, body lines 443-461, gives only the descriptive contrast); the problems qualifying the axioms and the theorem: P5 as motivated by Sections 2-3 'especially Theorem 3.2' (pp. 263-264), P6 (syntactic notions of L*-finite and L*-recursive, p. 264) and the added-in-proof P7 (extend 3.2 to conclude L* included in L# and improve 3.4 to a natural equivalence of L* with L_omega-omega, with the natural-transformation definitions, p. 264). (6) Qualifications attached to the notions of the proof bridge are absent: Sigma-1-1 versus PC classes and their equivalence modulo finite structures for L_omega-omega (p. 249); the consequence of 1.2 that (omega,<) is Sigma-1-1 iff omega is accessible, the counterexample L_omega-omega(Q^(WO)) for general alpha, and the coincidence of definable and accessible ordinals for L_omega-omega (pp. 250-251); every logic of Part I, Section 1 (printed 'Section 0') is bounded except second-order logic, and L_infinity-omega is bounded but not bounded by any beta since every (alpha,<) is L_infinity-omega-definable (p. 252); Keisler's L(omega) and Barwise's absolute logics [2] have the Karp property, and Section 3 uses the Karp property to characterize sublogics of L_infinity-omega (pp. 254-255); the stated reason for redefining the quantifier rank of atomic formulas, with the S example, as needed for 3.4 (pp. 244-245); and the Section 10 claims that partial isomorphism is an equivalence relation, that 10.2 is due to Russell rather than Cantor (Grandy), and that 10.3 and 10.5 are due to Karp (pp. 244-245). (7) Barwise's own Definition 1.1(i) (witnessing 0-morphism the identity except possibly at V, pp. 248-249) is replaced by a widened notion (body lines 194-202), and Theorems 1.2, 1.4, 3.2 and 3.3 are stated only for the widened notion; their statements under Barwise's definition are not supplied and no argument shows that the two definitions give the same Sigma-1-1 classes of ordinals.

Complete this source-specific component at the fixed identity and bounded scope: supply every proof and prerequisite construction required by Barwise's axioms and the selected Lindstrom-theorem formulation/proof bridge, with its exact source language, model domain, cardinality and choice hypotheses. Missing: (1) the prerequisite construction that supplies new symbols of prescribed kinds and arities in every proof (annex lines 8-15; body lines 172-178; w02c-p02-003 body lines 319-326) rests on Lemma 4.3 cited in place of written steps: that an isomorphism of the category of languages is a one-one interpretation onto its target is not proved (Barwise proves 4.3 on p. 230 from Lemmas 2.2-2.3), and with only the composite of an inclusion defined it cannot be derived from the text's definitions; (2) no proofs of 7.2 for an arbitrary inclusion, 7.4 and 7.5(ii) (pp. 235-237); (3) Theorems 1.2, 1.4, 3.2 and 3.3 under Barwise's Definition 1.1(i) are not proved (only their versions for the widened Sigma-1-1 notion of body lines 194-202), so in particular the direction from the Karp property and Barwise's boundedness by kappa to L_kappa-omega as strong as L* is not established for his boundedness notion; (4) symmetric steps are not written: the back clause in the level step is given 'similarly' (annex line 370), the converse of the existential case is 'uses the back property' (annex line 419), the second pull-back is 'likewise' (annex line 503), and the verification of (Q8) is 'likewise' (annex line 615).

defect_observations: Correctness not assessed; recorded for review: body lines 200-202 state that the category axioms do not supply a copy of a language in which a chosen symbol takes a prescribed name. Clauses (i), (iii) and (iv) of 6.2 appear to give a renaming morphism into K with the symbol < adjoined (moving an existing < to a new symbol), after which the Translation Axiom turns a widened Sigma-1-1 witness into one of Barwise's form; if so the widening is unnecessary.

The 048 corollary (body lines 428-432) concludes L* equivalent to L_omega-omega only when the symbols of chi with V form a language of the category; the unconditional formulation of 3.4 is thm:p02-w02c-p02-003-b74-lindstrom (w02c-p02-003 body lines 405-421), proved there by a different route.
